title: core: report the release of a tracked click on a prompt
body:
When the cursor is at a prompt with click-to-move (OSC 133 [click_events](https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/shell-integration/#notes-for-shell-developers) or [cl=](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/Per_Bothner/specifications/blob/master/proposals/semantic-prompts.md)) and a program started from that prompt tracks the mouse, a left click reaches the program as a press without a release (the release is instead replaced by the prompt click).

A release whose press went to the program now goes to the program too, instead of becoming a prompt click.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Use [ghostty shell integration](https://ghostty.org/docs/features/shell-integration).
2. Use [fzf shell integration](https://junegunn.github.io/fzf/shell-integration/#setting-up-shell-integration), for example `source <(fzf --zsh)` under zsh. Tested with zsh; bash uses the same `cl=line` mark and fish uses `click_events=1`, so both should take the same path.
3. Press `Ctrl-R` to open the fzf history search.
4. Double click on a history item to select it.

Results:
- Before: The history item is not inserted into the shell prompt, since fzf only completes a double click on the release event it never receives.
- After: The history item is inserted into the shell prompt.

AI disclosure: Created with opus 5.5 through claude code. Reviewed and tested by me.
